claims.text: architecture-health-review.md records a quarterly review of Đơn Hàng, assumed to be the first one, after Sprint 24; it asks whether existing decisions still hold; an ADR can stop holding while nobody edits it: its assumptions change while its text and every check guarding it stay the same.

ADR 0021 'Chưa dùng service mesh' (accepted); assumption 'Một nhóm, ba service .NET', signal: services from many groups or languages, seen at a new service proposed by ADR; review: three teams, still three .NET services; look again when DonHang.Support (ADR 0032 chat service, not built) is built.

claims.text: Seven inputs: governance watched table, 'Chưa có phép kiểm tự động' of fitness-functions.md, tech-debt-register.md estimates, slo.md SLOs, postmortem action items, delivery-metrics.md, design-review open questions; the watched table is read against docs/adr/README.md.

The review does not reopen or write ADRs; each row read ends in one choice: keep, add a check, put on the roadmap, or propose a new ADR replacing the old one; a row with no choice is written 'Mở' so everyone sees it.

'Chưa thấy' is a checked, recorded result, not a guess; rows whose signal cannot be measured yet are written 'Chưa đo được' (ADR 0022 provider fee, ADR 0024 delivery rate and price) and kept; only the fee row (no managed cluster bill) and delivery row (no real email from production) give a reason.
Rule when a signal appears: the watcher proposes a new ADR replacing the old; an accepted ADR is not edited to match, only its status changes to 'Bị thay thế bởi NNNN' (docs/adr/README.md).
All inputs exist before the meeting, so it is short; the architect role's part is reading them side by side, which no single team's document does.
This quarter no signal appeared, so no row led to a new or superseding ADR.

Known gaps: asks only for a roadmap.md item and an owner by role. No Prometheus in production: has H3 and owner (kept); staging alerts not sent to on-call: no item → roadmap with H3. H-labels name the technical-strategy.md action a roadmap item serves (H3: monitor production).

claims.text: Results: table lacks rows for ADRs 0004, 0013-0018, 0023, 0025, 0026-0033 → 'Thêm dòng vào bảng', team lead; scanning row 'Mở', two options next session; A1-A3 (app-experience.md) → roadmap; N2 → roadmap when accounting confirms; every row has choice, owner, next look.

Every check in fitness-functions.md runs on a change (push, pull request, new Pod), none on a schedule; a check sees only what it tests; a vulnerability published after an image was built is unseen until the next change; Grype scans only at build.

The running-image vulnerability gap is accepted until production because no environment before production (lab, staging) holds real customer data; it is to be reviewed when production takes customers.

Watchers by role: ADR 0020 data-region and ADR 0022 'contract demands own machines or data in one place' → product owner; ADR 0024 delivery rate and 'Dịch vụ A stops accepting SMTP' → backend developer; ADR 0012 'contract demands a separate copy' → product owner.

The governance table is reviewed each quarter together with technical-strategy.md and roadmap.md: add new ADRs with reopen conditions, check which signals appeared, check the decision-rights table against the number of teams.

An accepted ADR is not rewritten; when the decision changes a new ADR records it and the old one only changes status to 'Bị thay thế bởi NNNN' with a link, keeping its reasons as they were (why the choice was right at the time).

A quarterly review reading kept inputs fits when several teams keep their own documents and ADRs name reopen signals; relying on watchers alone fits a small team where every accepted ADR has its rows (opposing view).

When a shop's contract demands its data stay in one region, both the ADR 0020 and ADR 0022 rows (watcher: product owner) lead to proposing a superseding ADR; neither ADR's text changes; the review does not decide what the new ADRs say.
Each debt in the register carries an estimate of interest per quarter and principal, in hours.
